keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Heroic Australian pub-rock anthem in C major built around the universal I - V - vi - IV progression
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: A minor is the relative minor of C major

mainProgression.description: The ultimate heroic four-chord progression: grounding the tonic in C, driving through G, dipping into the relative minor Am, before rising triumphant on F.

sectionProgressions.description: Relentless four-chord cycle building from an intimate acoustic whisper to an explosive stadium singalong
Minor detour through Dm and F adding narrative tension before the triumphant final chorus return

harmonicFunction: C (I) - Triumphant major tonic establishing the hero's quest and home foundation
G (V) - Dominant chord propelling the momentum forward with urgency
Am (vi) - Relative minor introducing adversity, emotional gravity, and reflection
F (IV) - Majestic subdominant lift providing the uplifting resolution at the end of each four-bar phrase
Dm (ii) - Supertonic minor introducing contrast in the reflective bridge

techniques.name: Stadium Anthem Strumming & Dynamic Arc
techniques.description: Building from a quiet, palm-muted acoustic verse to thunderous open-string stadium strums with full dynamic swing

sequence: Start the verse with delicate down-up acoustic strums near the bridge
Accent beats 2 and 4 to sync with the kick-and-snare backbeat
Unleash full-arm strums across all 6 strings when the horns and drums enter on the chorus
tips: If the full F barre chord is difficult, use the open Fmaj7 (X-X-3-2-1-0) or mini-barre (X-X-3-2-1-1)
Keep your strumming wrist relaxed to maintain steady 120 BPM pocket for 4 minutes
Dig in heavily on the G to Am transition to highlight the emotional minor shift

sections.name: Verse Dynamic Build
sections.description: Intimate acoustic guitar establishing the legendary C - G - Am - F progression.
notes: Clean transitions between open C, G, and Am
Let the F chord ring out cleanly into the next measure

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Explosion
sections.description: Huge singalong explosion on 'And if you told me about the places you were goin' to...'.
notes: Lock firmly into the 120 BPM marching tempo

beginner.title: Mastering the Four Chords
steps: Learn open C, G, Am, and F (or Fmaj7)
Practice smooth transitions at 90 BPM with a metronome
Memorize the I - V - vi - IV sequence
beginner.goals: Smooth chord changes without pauses or buzzing strings

intermediate.title: Dynamic Arc & Strumming Energy
steps: Build from quiet verse finger-strumming to full stadium chorus power
Lock into 120 BPM using our Metronome tool
Clean up the barre on the full F major chord
intermediate.goals: Compelling live performance capturing Mark Seymour's raw intensity

advanced.title: Horn Section Guitar Emulation
steps: Learn the soaring electric guitar octave lines reinforcing the brass fanfare
Master the driving syncopated rhythm accents in the bridge
Perform the complete song with vocal singalong projection
advanced.goals: Stage-ready live performance of Australia's definitive sporting & pub anthem

commonMistakes: Starting the verse too loudly, leaving no room to build into the chorus
Struggling with the jump from Am to the full F major barre chord
Rushing past the 120 BPM tempo during the emotional climax
practiceRoutine: Warm up with 5 minutes of C - G - Am - F changes with a metronome
Practice the Am to F transition 15 times cleanly
Play through the entire track focusing on dynamic control from verse 1 to the final outro
focusAreas: Clean F major barre chord fretting
metronomeWork: Set click to 100 BPM to ensure clean chord landings on beat 1
Ramp up to 120 BPM with our Metronome Speed Trainer
Practice keeping steady time through the bridge without rushing
